入場料 (にゅうじょうりょう, nyūjōryō) means "entrance fee," and いりますか (irimasu ka) asks if something is required.
入場[にゅうじょう]料[りょう]は いくらですか？
How much is the entrance fee?
鼠,Questions

Do you cook?
鼠,Small Talk
料理[りょうり]は けっこう しますよ。
I cook quite a bit.
鼠,Small Talk
料理[りょうり]は よく 作[つく]りますよ。
I cook often.
鼠,Chitchat
ベジタリアン用[よう]の 料理[りょうり]が ありますか？
Do you have vegetarian dishes?
Travel
ベジタリアン用 (bejitarian-yō) means "for vegetarians," 料理 (ryōri) means "dishes," and ありますか (arimasu ka) is a polite way of asking "Is there?"
この 料理[りょうり]は 人気[にんき]ですか？
Is this dish popular?
鼠,Questions
以上[いじょう]で よろしいですか？
Is this all right?
Travel
以上 (ijou) means "above" or "this is all." よろしい (yoroshii) is a polite form of よい (yoi), meaning "good" or "acceptable." ですか (desu ka) turns the sentence into a polite question.
料理[りょうり]が まだ 来[き]ていません
The food hasn't come yet.
Travel

料理 (ryōri) means "food" or "dish." が (ga) is the subject marker, indicating that "food" is the subject of the sentence. まだ (mada) means "yet" or "still," implying that something has not happened up to that point. 来ていません (kite imasen) is the negative form of 来る (kuru), meaning "to come," with いません (imasen) being the polite negative ending. This phrase politely informs that the food has not arrived yet.
まだ 料理[りょうり]が 来[き]ていません。
My order hasn't arrived yet.
鼠,Daily
料金[りょうきん]は いくらですか?
How much is the fare?
Travel
料金 (りょうきん, ryōkin) means "fare," and いくらですか (ikura desu ka) means "how much?"
料金[りょうきん]は いくらですか？
How much is the rate?
鼠,Daily
料金[りょうきん]は おいくらですか？
How much is the fare?
Travel
料金 (りょうきん, ryōkin) means "fare" or "charge." おいくら (oikura) means "how much" in a polite form. です (desu) is the copula, and か (ka) turns it into a question.
ラッピング 料金[りょうきん]は いくらですか？

好[す]きじゃないです
I don't like (polite)
Travel
A polite version of "I don't like." The negative form じゃない (janai) is made polite by adding です (desu).

Travel

The verb 話せます (hanasemasu) is the polite form of the potential verb, meaning "can speak." All verbs when conjuated into the potential "can" form use the が particle even if they would usually use the を particle.
英語[えいご]が 話[はな]せますか
Can you speak English?
Travel
The question form of the sentence, asking if someone can speak English. The か (ka) particle turns the statement into a question.
英語[えいご]を 話[はな]せますか？
Can you speak English?
